what_this_is: FIRST Pareto frontier in the corpus with MEASURED execution per representation. Every prior Gravity receipt carried tps_specimen, a per-specimen CONSTANT identical across all variants (O003=51.627 for q2-g32-experts, mixed-q2q3, q4-g128 and q4-g64 alike). No variant had ever been executed. These four were.
REPRODUCES_EXISTING_ACCOUNTING: q2-g32-experts complete_bytes 6283610368 EXACTLY matches receipts/**/O003_GRAVITY_q2-g32-experts.json live_bytes/disk_tensor_bytes 6283610368; EBPW 3.0637 vs its 3.0639. The byte accounting in the 55 Gravity receipts is INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CORRECT. Only their TPS column was never a measurement.

FINDINGS.1_tps_rises_as_bytes_fall: 73.63 -> 81.65 -> 98.24 -> 100.01 tok/s as complete EBPW falls 15.56 -> 8.27 -> 4.38 -> 3.06. +35.8% decode for 5.08x fewer bytes. S006's claim that EBPW and TPS correlate is CONFIRMED on this specimen: decode is bandwidth-bound, so bytes ARE the speed.
FINDINGS.2_the_gain_saturates_at_q4: q8->q4 buys +20.3% TPS for 1.89x fewer bytes. q4->q2-experts buys only +1.8% TPS for a further 1.43x. The knee is q4-g64. Below it, bytes keep falling and TPS stops responding - so sub-bit work must be justified by RESIDENCY (fitting more/bigger models) not by decode speed.
FINDINGS.3_capability_cost_is_not_linear: ppl 2.894 -> 2.887 -> 3.044 -> 3.553. q8 is FREE (2.887 < 2.894, within noise). q4 costs +5.2%. q2-experts costs +22.8%. The capability cliff and the TPS knee are at the SAME place (q4).
FINDINGS.4_prefill_is_flat: 2485 -> 2804 -> 2803 -> 2789 tok/s. Prefill is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound, so it gains once (dequant path) then ignores further byte reduction entirely.

NEGATIVE_CONTROLS_THAT_FIRED: Run 1: predicate accepted only nn.Linear/nn.Embedding. q4-g64 and q2-g32-experts returned BYTE-IDENTICAL results (29756639488) and identical NLL - the 78 SwitchLinear modules holding 26.81 of 29.72 GiB (90.2%) were silently skipped. Two configs agreeing to the byte is the tell.

Run 2: a bad edit deleted the dispatch block, so quantize() never ran. arrays stayed 430 (the bf16 count) and complete_bytes equalled bf16 exactly. Fixed by adding `assert nq>0, 'PREDICATE MATCHED NOTHING'` so a no-op can never again be reported as a result.
Run 3 (this one): quantized modules = 296 for all three configs, arrays 430 -> 1022.
CAVEATS: ppl is measured on ONE fixed 512-token passage. It is a capability PROXY, not a capability eval. It ranks these four consistently but must not be quoted as a benchmark score.
bf16 decode measured 73.63 here vs 69.97 in O003_TPS_BASELINE.json - 5.2% run-to-run spread. Treat differences under ~6% as noise; the 35.8% headline is well outside it.
Quantization is post-hoc affine (mx.quantize), no calibration data. A calibrated method would likely move the capability column, not the byte or TPS columns.
